name: Gabonese Poulet Nyembwe
description: Poulet nyembwe, chicken stewed in real palm nut sauce, is widely considered Gabon's national dish - real palm nut cream isn't a distinct item here, so peanut butter stands in for a similarly rich, reddish sauce.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, then add to the pot.
Simmer 25-28 minutes until the chicken is very tender.

name: Gabonese Saka Saka
description: Saka saka, pounded cassava leaves simmered with peanut, a genuine Gabonese staple shared across the wider Congo Basin - real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter with a little water, then add the spinach.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until well combined.

name: Gabonese Fufu
description: Fufu, cassava pounded into a smooth, stretchy dough, is one of Gabon's most essential staple starches.
steps_detailed: Boil the cassava until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Drain and pound vigorously until smooth and stretchy.

name: Gabonese Liboke
description: Liboke, fish seasoned and wrapped in banana leaf to steam in its own juices, a genuine cooking technique shared across Central Africa.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and ginger.
Wrap tightly in foil.
Bake at 400F (200C) for 20-22 minutes until just cooked through, sealed in its own steam.
